# Caribe (01, engineer) — BAD-029

## Brief
Objective: Turn the ad-hoc dry run of the "Set the profiles_web password" step in `.github/workflows/server-deploy.yml` into a real test, `test/server/deploy-step.test.mjs`, that runs under `npm test` (and so in ci.yml on every PR) and pins the step's *behaviour*, not its text: which URL reaches psql, that the role password travels as `-v pw=<secret>` and the superuser's as `PGPASSWORD`, that the ALTER arrives on psql's stdin (never `-c`), and that the step exits 0 in every branch by design.

Why: the step never fails the job on purpose (its own comment explains: a failing step between `db push` and the function deploy would strand production on the new schema with the old functions). That contract made two real bugs invisible in CI: run 34926953514 wrote nothing because an unchanged URL was treated as an error (fixed in #349), and run 34927908869 sent `:'pw'` through `-c`, which psql never substitutes (fixed in #350). Both were proven locally with a stub psql in under a second; that harness should be a committed test.

Read first:
- `.github/workflows/server-deploy.yml`, the whole "Set the profiles_web password" step and the comments around it — the comments are the spec.
- The proposer's harness, which you are porting to node:test: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ericlugo-Personal-BadTakes/32d19997-5c89-4794-b49e-16c300a19e7a/scratchpad/dryrun.sh` (extraction + eight cases with a stub psql that echoes its argv and stdin), and `failbranch.sh` beside it (a psql that exits 3 must take the else branch and the step still exits 0). `realpg.sh` there is a real-Postgres proof; NOT in scope, do not port it.
- `test/server/schema.test.mjs` and `test/server/admin-moderation.test.mjs` for the house shape: `node:test` + `node:assert`, paths resolved from `import.meta.url`, a comment on each test saying which rule it pins and why.
- `server/README.md` § the profiles_web password (search `profiles_web`) for the documented contract.

Design, decided:
1. Extract the step body from the YAML at test time by line-slicing, the way dryrun.sh does (find `- name: Set the profiles_web password`, assert the next line is `run: |`, take the 10-space-indented block, dedent). No YAML library: `js-yaml` is only a transitive dependency here, not declared, and this repo adds no dependency for a test. Fail loudly (assert) if the step is not found or not a `run: |` block, so a rename of the step breaks this test rather than vacuously passing.
2. Run the body with `bash -e <file>` (GitHub's default `run:` shell is `bash -e {0}`), via `node:child_process` `spawnSync`, cwd set to a per-test temp dir laid out like the job's `server/` working directory (`<tmp>/server/supabase/.temp/pooler-url`), with `PATH` prefixed by a stub dir. Use `fs.mkdtempSync` under `os.tmpdir()` and clean up.
3. Stub `psql` is an executable bash script in the stub dir that prints `PGPASSWORD=<len>`, each argv, and every stdin line, and exits with a code the test chooses (0 by default; 3 for the failure-branch case). Stub `command -v psql` finds it because it is first on PATH. For the "no psql" case, run with a PATH containing only the stub dir with no psql in it and whatever is needed for `tr`, `printf` — simplest: a PATH of the stub dir plus `/usr/bin:/bin` and no stub psql, on a runner where psql is not installed in /usr/bin; if `/usr/bin/psql` exists on the machine (it may on a dev Mac), skip that one sub-test with a reason rather than fail.
4. Cases to pin, each asserting on the stub's captured output and the step's stdout/stderr/exit code:
   - real CLI-2.114.0 URL (no password field) → psql called with exactly that URL as argv[1], `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, `-v pw=<the secret>`, `-q`, no `-c` anywhere in argv, stdin is exactly `alter role profiles_web with password :'pw';`, PGPASSWORD length equals the superuser secret's length, stdout says "profiles_web's password is set", exit 0.
   - literal `:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@` and percent-encoded `:%5BYOUR-PASSWORD%5D@` placeholders → stripped, psql sees the clean URL, exit 0.
   - not the pooler host and carrying a password → no psql call, `::error::` on stdout containing `not the Supavisor pooler`, the redacted form `//***@`, and NOT the password string, exit 0.
   - two lines in the file → no psql call, `::error::` mentioning whitespace, exit 0.
   - not a URL (`Access token not provided.`) → no psql call, `::error::` mentioning `not a postgresql:// URL`, exit 0.
   - pooler-url missing → no psql call, `::error::` naming the file, exit 0.
   - PROFILES_DB_PASSWORD empty → no psql call, `::warning::` naming `PROFILES_DB_PASSWORD` and the `gh secret set` command, exit 0.
   - psql exits 3 → the else branch: `::error::could not set profiles_web's password (exit 3)`, and exit 0. Pin that the reported exit is psql's (3), not printf's (0): that is what `set -o pipefail` buys.
   - no psql on PATH → `::error::no psql on this runner`, exit 0 (skip with a reason if the host has a system psql outside the stub dir; see 3).
   Never put a real-looking secret in the fixtures; use obviously fake values and assert the "password" never appears in the step's output for the malformed-URL case.
5. Platform: `npm test` runs on windows-latest too (ci.yml `test-windows`). Skip the whole file's tests on `process.platform === 'win32'` with a reason (`bash` + a stub on PATH is a POSIX harness), and also skip when `bash` is not found. The test must pass on macOS (bash 3.2, the `${var/pattern/repl}` and `case` forms the step uses are bash 3 compatible; verify) and on ubuntu-latest.
6. Keep it one file, under ~200 lines of code, with a header comment saying what it pins and why the step's soft-fail contract makes this test the only red signal short of deploy-profiles.yml's /status probe. No changes to server-deploy.yml: if the step as written cannot pass a case above, that is a finding for your `member result`, not something to fix here (file a `proposal` if it is a real bug).

Setup: this is a fresh worktree on branch `chore/bad-029-deploy-step-test`. Run `bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` from the worktree root first (it installs node_modules; the voicepacks and smoke library it wires are irrelevant to this ticket).

Verification (the project's `implementing-changes` skill applies):
- `node --test test/server/deploy-step.test.mjs` green, every case listed above present and passing; quote the summary lines.
- Mutation check, so the test is not vacuous: temporarily change the step's stdin line back to a `-c "…"` form in a scratch copy, or point the test at a scratch YAML with that edit, and show the stdin/no-`-c` case fails; then restore. Same for the "unchanged URL is an error" regression from #349 if it is cheap to simulate. Quote the failing output in your result, and confirm `git diff --stat` shows only your deliverable at the end.
- `npm test` for the whole suite green (pack tests skip without voicepacks/; say so, do not claim they ran).

Done when: `test/server/deploy-step.test.mjs` exists, passes, would fail under the two historical bugs, the suite is green, `member log` records progress and `member result` records what you built with the verification output quoted.

## Ticket proposals
- **Share one 'extract a run: | step out of a workflow' helper between the two tests that do it** — suggested P3; created as [[BAD-033]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: test/release-workflow.test.js and the new test/server/deploy-step.test.mjs each carry their own YAML line-slicer for a workflow step's shell body. They are near-identical and already differ in tolerance (release-workflow scans forward for the run: | line and stops at the next step; deploy-step requires it on the very next line), so a third test that wants one will copy whichever it finds first. A shared test helper would make the strictness a decision rather than an accident.
  Evidence: test/release-workflow.test.js:29-46 stepScript(name); test/server/deploy-step.test.mjs:55-69 stepScript(workflow). Both read a workflow, find '- name: <step>', compute indent+2 and slice until the indentation drops.

NOTES
- The step as written passes every case in the brief; no bug found in it, nothing to fix there.
- Design deviation, deliberate and small: for the 'no psql on this runner' case the brief allowed skipping when the host has a system psql. Instead the harness resolves bash to an absolute path once and runs that case with PATH set to just the empty stub dir, so command -v psql cannot find anything. No skip is needed and the case also runs on ubuntu-latest, where /usr/bin/psql exists and a skip would have hidden it exactly where it matters. That branch is reached with shell builtins only, so an empty PATH is enough (a 'tr: command not found' there would mean the step grew work before its psql check — noted in a comment).
- Correction to one line of the brief: the reported '(exit 3)' does not depend on set -o pipefail. psql is the last command of the pipeline, so the pipeline status is psql's with or without it; pipefail matters in the other direction (a printf killed by SIGPIPE could turn a successful ALTER into a reported failure). The test pins the observable — exit 3 reported, step exits 0 — and the comment states it accurately rather than repeating the claim.
- bash 3.2 verified: 'bash' resolves to /bin/bash 3.2.57 on this Mac, so the green run above already executed the step's ${var/pattern/repl} and case *[[:space:]]* forms under bash 3.
- Filed proposal 60 (P3): release-workflow.test.js and this file each carry their own YAML step extractor, already differing in strictness.

Full suite green with packs present. The brief's pipefail remark was wrong, as Caribe noted; the test pins the observable exit code. No changes to the workflow.
